question: How many confirmed human West Nile virus cases will RIVM report in the Netherlands for 2026 as of its mid-October update?

calls.reasoning: Cumulative 56 as of the 1 Oct RIVM update. Two more Thursday updates (8 Oct, 15 Oct) fall in the window. Weekly increments were 9,9,10,16,12. RIVM says the peak has passed, and leading indicators fell sharply (horses +48 -> +14, no new mosquito pools). Human reports lag infection by 1-3 weeks, so increments continue but taper: about +5-10 then +2-7, giving a median near 69. No human prediction market was found (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi checked). Tails: a warm-autumn tail or batch late reports could push it higher; a missed update or no new cases could keep it lower.
calls.dossier:
- RIVM actueel page (rivm.nl/westnijlkoorts/actueel), weekly Thursday updates in 2026: 3 Sep total 9 cases (1 death); 10 Sep +9 -> 18; 17 Sep +10 -> 28 (4 deaths); 24 Sep +16 -> 44 (5 deaths); 1 Oct +12 -> 56 (9 deaths). Note: the question background says 28 on 10 Sep, but RIVM's page shows 18 on 10 Sep and 28 on 17 Sep.
- RIVM 1 Oct: 'expects we are past the peak of this outbreak, because the number of new infections has decreased in recent weeks.' Most patients were diagnosed after hospitalisation, which means a reporting lag of 1-3 weeks after infection.
- Animal surveillance (RIVM): new positive horses per week 53 (10 Sep), 30 (17 Sep), 48 (24 Sep), 14 (1 Oct); birds +33, +61, +71, +7; mosquito pools +1, 0, +1, 0 (4 total).
- Provinces at 1 Oct: Zuid-Holland 32, Utrecht 12, Noord-Holland 5, Noord-Brabant 4, Gelderland 2, Overijssel 1.
- GGD Hollands Midden (early Oct): house mosquitoes stay active in mild autumn weather; the GGD keeps advising bite protection.
- NL history: 8 human cases in 2020, none 2021-2025. 2026 is the first large outbreak.
- Status quo: total 56; further increments expected while reporting lags.
- Resolves off the RIVM cumulative total in the latest update on or before 16 Oct (expected Thursday 15 Oct). Not counted: deaths, animals, probable cases.
- Event window: updates of 8 Oct and 15 Oct are still to come; as of 5 Oct 14:40 UTC, none of the remaining updates has been published (the 1 Oct to 15 Oct span is about 35% elapsed).
- Market check: none found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi.
- Searched but not found: any case data after 1 Oct, onset-date epidemic curve, Dutch weather forecast for October.
calls.reference_class: Weekly cumulative human WNV case counts in European temperate-zone outbreaks after the declared peak (late Sep-Oct), e.g. the course of this outbreak's own increments and seasonal declines in Germany, the Netherlands and northern Italy

RIVM says the peak has passed, but reports lag onset by about 2-3 weeks because diagnosis mostly follows hospitalization, and horse cases were still rising (+14 in the week to 1 Oct), so late-September infections are still being reported. calls.reasoning: RIVM cumulative totals: 9 (3 Sep), 18 (10 Sep), 28 (17 Sep), 44 (24 Sep), 56 (1 Oct); weekly increments +9, +10, +16, +12. Two more Thursday updates (8 and 15 Oct) count before the deadline. RIVM says the peak has passed, and mosquito activity drops through October, which points to falling increments (~+8 then ~+5, giving ~69). But reporting lags (cases confirmed after hospitalization) and continued horse and bird detections (14 horses, 7 birds last week) keep a tail toward ~75-80. If RIVM skips an update or moves to fortnightly reporting, the total lands lower, ~60-66. No human prediction market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.

calls.reference_class: Trajectory of weekly increments after the peak in seasonal WNV outbreaks (this 2026 Dutch series, and European seasons such as Italy and Greece, where cases tail off over 3-6 weeks after the peak with reporting lags)

calls.reconciliation: Factual dispute: question background lists 28 cases on 10 Sep, whereas all three dossiers report RIVM's actueel page showing 18 (10 Sep) and 28 (17 Sep); accepted the RIVM sequence (increments +9,+10,+16,+12) as consistent across all runs. No other factual disputes; all runs agree on 56 at 1 Oct, two remaining updates, RIVM's post-peak statement, and the falling animal surveillance signals. Remaining differences (size of next two increments, tail weights) are judgment; evidence supports a median ~68 with a right-skewed tail. I agree with the runs' reference class and ~16 dispersion and carry them forward. No retrieval performed this run.
